rules.title: Hoboken rent control ordinance limits ordinary rent increases in covered units
rules.requirement: For dwelling units covered by Hoboken's rent control chapter, a landlord generally may not charge more than the lesser of 5% or the applicable CPI-based percentage at lease expiration or termination, and may not impose more than one such cost-of-living increase in any 12-month period. The chapter applies to all dwelling units unless a listed exemption applies, including certain newly constructed dwellings, buildings vacant since January 1, 1984, and certain post-1987 multiple dwellings exempt under state-authorized local exemption language incorporated into the code.
rules.key_value: lesser of 5% or applicable CPI percentage; no more than one such increase in any 12-month period

other_dates.quote: [Added 7-12-2000 by Ord. No. R-449; amended 9-6-2000 by Ord. No. R-455; 7-9-2025 by Ord. No. B-778; 10-22-2025 by Ord. No. B-818]

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to dwelling units as defined in the chapter.
coverage_conditions.quote: This chapter shall apply to all dwelling units as defined in § 155-1 above, except that the following shall be exempt:

coverage_conditions.value: lease expiration or termination; periodic tenancies also covered
coverage_conditions.text: Ordinary capped increases apply at lease expiration or termination, including periodic tenants and leases under one year.
coverage_conditions.quote: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of a lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord may request or receive a percentage increase in rent which is greater than 5% or the percentage difference between the consumer price index three months prior to the expiration or termination of the lease and three months prior to the commencement of the lease term, whichever is less. For a periodic tenant or for a tenant whose lease terms shall be less than one year, said tenant shall not suffer or be caused to pay more than one rent increase in any twelve-month period which exceeds 5% or the consumer price index percentage differential for the twelve-month period commencing 15 months prior to and ending three months prior to the effective date of the proposed increase, whichever is less.

exemptions.value: newly constructed dwellings first rented for the first time; initial rent/lease only if registered before first rental
exemptions.text: Newly constructed dwellings are exempt for the initial rent or lease agreement if registered before first rental; later rents are covered.
exemptions.quote: Newly constructed dwellings which are rented for the first time. After the first rental, such dwellings shall be exempt for this initial rent or lease agreement, but all subsequent rents shall be subject to the provisions of this chapter. In order to qualify for the exemption, the newly constructed dwelling must be registered by an applicant, on forms provided by the Rent Regulation Officer, with said Officer before the first rental for said dwelling.

exemptions.value: nonresidential and commercial property; mixed-use commercial portions only
exemptions.text: Nonresidential and commercial property is exempt, though apartment units in mixed-use buildings remain covered.
exemptions.quote: Nonresidential and commercial property. If the dwelling has an apartment unit(s), plus a commercial unit(s), the apartment unit(s) is covered by this chapter, but the commercial unit(s) is exempt.

exemptions.value: student housing owned or controlled by school/college/institution
exemptions.text: Student housing owned or controlled by an educational institution is exempt.
exemptions.quote: Housing provided for students by a school, college or similar institution which owns or controls that housing.

exemptions.text: Housing owned and operated by other government agencies is exempt.
exemptions.quote: Housing owned and operated by other government agencies, such as the state or federal government.

exemptions.value: building completely vacant on or before and since 1984-01-01 and not vacant through unlawful means; initial rent/lease only if registered before renting
exemptions.text: A building completely vacant on or before and since January 1, 1984 may qualify for an initial-rent exemption if not made vacant through unlawful means and registered before renting; later rents are covered.
exemptions.quote: A building completely vacant on or before and since January 1, 1984, provided that said building did not become vacant through unlawful means which can be attributed to the applicant for this exemption. In order to qualify for this exemption, the building vacant since January 1, 1984, must be registered by an applicant with the Rent Regulation Officer, on forms provided by said Officer, before the renting of dwelling units within the vacant building. After the first rental, such dwelling units shall be exempt from initial rent or lease agreement, but all subsequent rents shall be subject to the provisions of this chapter.

exemptions.text: Certain multiple dwellings constructed after June 25, 1987 are exempt for the amortization period of the initial mortgage or 30 years after completion, whichever is less, if statutory notice requirements are met.
exemptions.quote: In accordance with N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.1 et seq., the provisions of this chapter shall not apply to multiple dwellings, as defined in the statute, constructed after June 25, 1987, for a period not to exceed the period of amortization of any initial mortgage loan obtained for the multiple dwelling or for 30 years following completion of construction, whichever is less. In the event that there is no initial mortgage financing, the period of exemption from this chapter shall be 30 years. This exemption only applies where a landlord complied with all requirements contained in N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.1 et seq., including but not limited to notice to the Construction Code Official at least 30 days before a certificate of occupancy is issued and notification to tenants by way of a provision in their lease.

exemptions.value: governmental agency contract preempts city regulation during contract period
exemptions.text: Where a governmental agency contract supersedes Hoboken's authority to regulate rents, the chapter is preempted during that contract period.
exemptions.quote: If a contract between a landlord and a governmental agency duly provides for that governmental agency to regulate the amount of rent received by that landlord, and if the authority of that governmental agency supersedes the authority of the City of Hoboken to regulate such rents, then the application of this chapter shall be preempted during the period of governmental agency regulation specified in the contract.

For a periodic tenant or for a tenant whose lease terms shall be less than one year, said tenant shall not suffer or be caused to pay more than one rent increase in any twelve-month period which exceeds 5% or the consumer price index percentage differential for the twelve-month period commencing 15 months prior to and ending three months prior to the effective date of the proposed increase, whichever is less.

rules.title: Hoboken rent control ordinance defines just cause for eviction by reference to state law
rules.requirement: For tenancies covered by Hoboken's rent control chapter, 'just cause for eviction' means the landlord recovered possession for one of the reasons outlined in New Jersey state law. The city documents here do not provide the operative local eviction procedures, notices, or relocation assistance beyond that definition.
rules.key_value: Causes are those in N.J.S.A. 2A:18-53, as amended

rules.rule_quote: JUST CAUSE FOR EVICTIONThe landlord recovered possession of a housing space or dwelling for one of the reasons outlined in New Jersey State law (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-53 as amended).

finding_note: The provided Hoboken city documents do not contain a Hoboken-enacted or Hoboken-proposed security deposit rule setting a maximum amount or exception. The only mention is definitional: Chapter 155 states, "Security deposits and charges for accessories, such as boats, mobile homes and automobiles not used in connection with the housing space, shall not be construed as 'rent.'" That is not a security-deposit maximum rule for this category. No Hoboken bill or ordinance in these documents regulates security deposit amount.

The provided Hoboken city documents cover rent increases, rent control applicability, and algorithmic rent fixing, but do not contain any Hoboken provision on tenant-paid application or screening fees, fee caps, receipts/refunds, or broker/finder fees charged to tenants.

The provided Hoboken city documents cover rent increases, algorithmic rent fixing, and rent control applicability/increase procedures. They do not contain Hoboken screening restrictions on criminal-history screening, source-of-income screening, or screening timing rules.

rules.title: Algorithmic rent fixing in rental housing market prohibited
rules.requirement: Hoboken prohibits landlords from using software, algorithms, or data-sharing platforms to coordinate, recommend, or implement residential rents, lease terms, or occupancy levels using nonpublic competitor information. Violations may be enforced by the Division of Housing or an aggrieved private citizen in Municipal Court and may be punished by fines up to $2,000 or community service up to 90 days.
rules.key_value: Algorithmic pricing using nonpublic competitor information is prohibited; fine up to $2,000
rules.stage_quote:
Article II
Algorithmic Rent Fixing in Rental Housing Market
[Adopted 7-9-2025 by Ord. No. B-781]

effective.quote:
Hoboken, NJ
Hoboken City Code, ch. 158-2 (effective July 2025)
Prohibits landlords from using software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms to coordinate or recommend rents, lease terms, or occupancy.

coverage_conditions.value: residential dwelling unit used as a primary residence
coverage_conditions.text: Applies to landlords who rent residential dwelling units used as primary residences in Hoboken.
coverage_conditions.quote: Landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit (defined as any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities) in the City of Hoboken are prohibited from price fixing using algorithmic pricing.

exemptions.value: medical/long-term care or detention facilities excluded
exemptions.text: Excludes medical, long-term care, and detention facilities from the definition of residential dwelling unit.
exemptions.quote: Landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit (defined as any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities) in the City of Hoboken are prohibited from price fixing using algorithmic pricing.

rules.penalty: Upon conviction, penalties may include those prescribed under N.J.S.A. 40:49-5, a fine not exceeding $2,000, or community service not exceeding 90 days.
rules.rule_quote: Landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit (defined as any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities) in the City of Hoboken are prohibited from price fixing using algorithmic pricing. For purposes of this chapter, "price fixing using algorithmic pricing" shall be defined as the use of software, algorithms, or data-sharing platforms to collect and analyze nonpublic competitor information from other real estate lessors in order to coordinate, recommend, or implement rental prices, lease terms, or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units among competing real estate lessors.
